newsitem.title: FRANCE: SIDO sees higher French 1996 rapeseed crop.
newsitem.headline: SIDO sees higher French 1996 rapeseed crop.

text.p: France may produce more rapeseed in 1996 than in 1995, mostly due to higher sowings and steady yields, the French oilseeds and protein seeds association SIDO said on Wednesday .
SIDO had predicted in June a lower rapeseed crop, forecasting at the time a decline in yields.
In its second estimate for the 1996/97 campaign, SIDO raised its output target to 2.8 million tonnes from 2.5 million in June and the 2.7 million produced in 1995/96.
The new estimate assumes area rose to 865,000 hectares from 845,000.
The national yield is seen unchanged from its 1995/96 level of 3.2 tonnes.
The amount of set-aside land used for growing rapeseed for industrial use was seen down 35 percent to 215,000 ha, resulting in a production of 650,000 tonnes against 950,000 last year.
Firm rapeseed prices and ample oil stocks may reduce crushings to 800,000 tonnes from 1.01 million tonnes in 1995/96.
A poor rapeseed crop in Germany and a decline in Canadian production may benefit French exports, SIDO said.
Total exports may increase to 1.7 million tonnes from 1.3 million last year.
France would end the 1996/97 season with rapeseed stocks of 48,000 tonnes against 68,000.
